answer: A registry can charge each new agent a small stake that grows only with verified work. The stake starts at the size of a juniper berry, cheap, but an identity cannot vote or claim rewards until it finishes a chain of jobs. Each job result is sealed with a cipher tied to the agent's key, so one operator running a thousand clones must still pay for a thousand jobs of compute. A clone that tries to wander off and re-register to dodge a bad reputation forfeits the stake and starts over at zero. Sybils stay possible in theory, but each one costs as much as the honest work it pretends to do.
